candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP), an inflammatory/fibrotic lung disease. Lung cancer is a neoplastic entity and represents a differential diagnosis rather than the same diagnostic object. While multifocal consolidation can be seen in both, and lung cancer (particularly adenocarcinoma with lepidic spread) is a reasonable differential in this clinical scenario, it asserts an incompatible diagnostic category and etiology compared to COP.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Lung cancer is a distinct neoplastic entity; multifocal consolidation pattern overlaps but the diagnostic category conflicts with cryptogenic organizing pneumonia

case_quality_flags: Clinical scenario is classic for COP: subacute dry cough, antibiotic-unresponsive consolidation, negative infectious workup, empirical TB therapy failure
Lung cancer (especially adenocarcinoma in situ/lepidic pattern) is a legitimate differential but not the reference diagnosis
Biopsy planned — final diagnosis would require histopathology confirmation
